tldr: SELF is a framework that enables LLMs to autonomously self-improve through iterative self-evolution using language-based feedback, without human intervention or external reward models.
contributions: Introduces SELF (Self-Evolution with Language Feedback) framework for autonomous LLM evolution
Demonstrates self-refinement can be facilitated in smaller LLMs (Vicuna-7b), previously considered emergent only in top-tier large LLMs
Shows effectiveness in both mathematical and general domains through experiments
methods: SELF first teaches meta-skills (self-feedback and self-refinement) via fine-tuning on a curated meta-skill training corpus D_meta using cross-entropy loss. Then, in an iterative self-evolution process, the model generates initial responses from unlabeled prompts, refines them through self-feedback and self-refinement, filters out low-quality data via self-feedback, and uses the refined data for subsequent self-evolution training iterations. The framework also supports self-refinement during inference. The experiments used Vicuna-7b as the base model.
results: SELF improved test accuracy by 6.82% on GSM8K and 4.9% on SVAMP in mathematical domains. It increased win rate by 10% on Vicuna testset and 6.9% on Evol-Instruct testset in general domains, compared with typical supervised fine-tuning.
limitations: The meta-skill learning phase requires GPT-4 as the language model labeler to construct the initial training corpus. Self-refinement during inference requires multi-turn inference, leading to increased computational overhead. The framework's effectiveness is evaluated only on mathematical and general domains, with limited evidence of generalizability to other domains.
